body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Sunday, August 23, 2026 — a day that’s already seen its share of difficult news. Overnight, a shooting outside a Taco Bell in east Bakersfield left one person wounded, and a fire broke out at a vacant house on King Street. Today’s weather will be hot and clear, with a high near 103° and air quality at a moderate 64. Our thoughts are with those affected by last night’s violence as we look ahead to a week of community events and meetings.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious call came just after midnight, when a witness reported seeing someone shot at a Taco Bell in the Baker Street area. Officers responded with an officer-safety broadcast after the witness described the suspect as a white male in his 40s to 50s, wearing a black shirt and dark pants, sitting inside a white vehicle — possibly a Ford Explorer. Earlier, around 2:16 a.m., flames were visible inside a vacant single-story house on King Street with heavy smoke showing. Multiple engines and a truck company responded, and the fire was under control by about 2:25. Just before 11 p.m., a two-vehicle collision near Gosford Road and Harris Road left one vehicle on fire. Engine 14 and Engine 9 responded — one car was smoking with another about a quarter mile back — and command dubbed it the Harris Incident. Injuries from that collision are unknown. Multiple reports of a grass fire drew a large response along southbound Highway 395 north of Brown Road, but crews found a small roadside fire that was quickly extinguished, and the extra equipment was canceled. Around 10:38 p.m., an assault with a knife was reported with no injuries. The suspect — about 6 feet tall with neck tattoos, wearing black shorts, a gray shirt and white shoes — fled on foot northbound.

## Today's weather

Today will be hot and clear, with a high near 103° and a low around 74° tonight. It’s currently 73° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and there are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is at a moderate 64. Stay cool and hydrated if you’re heading out today.

## Top stories

**Bakersfield Now reports that Southwest Market has canceled its Saturday event at Independence High School after a fatal shooting.** The decision came after a deadly incident at the school’s football game, where a 15-year-old suspect was arrested miles away from the scene. The cancellation highlights the community’s shock and concern over the violence. 

**According to 23ABC, a 26-year-old man was shot and killed at a McFarland laundromat on Saturday afternoon.** Officers responded to the Capri Laundromat on Perkins Avenue around 3:18 p.m. and found the victim suffering from multiple gunshot wounds inside the laundromat. Despite immediate medical aid and CPR, the victim was pronounced dead at the scene. Preliminary information indicates two unknown suspects arrived at the Capri Liquors, which is adjacent to the laundromat, and confronted the victim inside. An argument led to one of the suspects producing a firearm and shooting the victim multiple times. The suspects then fled the area in an unknown vehicle. No suspects have been identified, no arrests have been made, and the motive remains unknown. The victim’s identity will be released after next of kin have been notified. 

**KGET 17 tells us that Bakersfield Mayor Karen Goh has released a statement on the deadly shooting at Independence High School.** Mayor Goh expressed her condolences to the victim’s family and friends and emphasized that the city is working closely with law enforcement to ensure the safety of all residents. The statement comes as the community grapples with the aftermath of the violence.

## Something good

In a heartwarming display of community support, a family is hosting a Saturday flea market to raise funds for a prosthetic leg for Villafana. The event aims to collect $8,900 to support this important cause. It’s a reminder of the kindness and generosity that make Kern County a special place to call home.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, there are several public meetings and events worth noting. On Wednesday, August 26, a Special City Council Meeting will take place at 12:00 p.m., followed by City Council Meeting 330 at 3:30 p.m. and City Council Meeting 515 at 5:15 p.m. 

For entertainment, the Fox Theater has a full lineup this week. On Tuesday, August 24, you can catch the Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027. Comedian Rodney Carrington will take the stage on Friday, August 27. On Saturday, August 28, enjoy the CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE. Willie Barcena will perform on Sunday, August 29, and later that evening, the Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix will take place. Finally, on Friday, September 4, the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA will come to town. 

It’s a week of both serious business and community fun — stay safe and enjoy the events that interest you.
